schema.authority: Authoritative machine-readable form of the ROM-editor coverage census. docs/research/ROM_EDITOR_COVERAGE_LEDGER.md renders this file; docs/research/ROM_EDITOR_SYSTEM_CENSUS.md carries the evidence narrative; docs/research/ROM_EDITOR_COVERAGE_SUMMARY.md carries the decisions.
schema.determinism: Rows are grouped by area in a fixed order (MAP/WORLD, ENTITIES/GAMEPLAY, SCRIPT/TEXT, GRAPHICS, AUDIO, SYSTEM/ROM) and hold the order the census enumerated them. Every list is sorted where it is a set of names. No timestamp, host path or run-specific value is stored. Every count in totals and rom_surface is recomputed from rows by tests/unit/test_rom_editor_coverage.py, which fails on any difference; no count is authored by hand.

fields.rows[].id: stable census id, kebab-case, unique across the file
fields.rows[].area: MAP/WORLD | ENTITIES/GAMEPLAY | SCRIPT/TEXT | GRAPHICS | AUDIO | SYSTEM/ROM
fields.rows[].games.<game>.state: one of vocabularies.coverage_states; the row's current top-level coverage state for that title
fields.rows[].games.<game>.basis: MEASURED (this title was investigated and the cell is supported by evidence) | NOT_INVESTIGATED (no adequate evidence for this title exists; the state is a statement about this lab, not about the game)
fields.rows[].read|edit|author|xref|raw_range|v: row-level prose; each names the title when the titles differ
fields.facilities[]: generic ROM-editor facilities. Deliberately NOT part of denominator.accepted_rows: a facility is a product capability, not a game system.
fields.totals: computed strictly from rows[].games; a cell whose state is N_A is excluded from that title's denominator. by_area_buus_fury counts this title's cells only, so its state columns sum to its row count.

schema.aggregate_rule: The family-wide aggregate counts (row, game) cells, not rows: one cell per row per title. A cell whose state is N_A is excluded from both numerator and denominator. Because the state vocabulary is ordinal only for FULLY_EDITABLE and PARTIALLY_EDITABLE (the two states in which the product can write), the only aggregate percentage published is writable_cells / measured_cells; the five state counts are published separately per title and never summed into one score.

capability_registry.note: Read, not modified. This registry is not this denominator and was not recomputed into one.

coverage_state_definitions.FULLY_EDITABLE: Inspectable, safely editable, validated against known-invalid writes, persisted through project and build, not restricted to a subset that materially changes ordinary hacking of that system, and observed in the governed emulator; where a runtime observation is impossible for the domain, the state is PARTIALLY_EDITABLE with that reason stated.
coverage_state_definitions.PARTIALLY_EDITABLE: The product can semantically modify the system and material restrictions remain; the restriction is named numerically where a number exists.
coverage_state_definitions.SEMANTIC_READ_ONLY: The product identifies and displays the system and no semantic write path reaches it. Raw hex editing does not count.
coverage_state_definitions.KNOWN_BUT_UNSUPPORTED: The system is identified and bounded enough to say what it is, and the product has no semantic model for it.
coverage_state_definitions.UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED: An editor-relevant region or system is known or plausibly held to exist and its semantic role or boundary is not understood well enough to classify it, or it has been measured only as a negative over declared tables. A measured negative is not a proven boundary.
coverage_state_definitions.N_A: Evidence shows the system genuinely does not exist in that title.

denominator.definition: One row per coherent editor-relevant semantic domain: a structure, resource family or engine system whose support can meaningfully be classified, with a boundary that evidence supports. A row is not a map, not a function, not a capability and not a UI surface. Rows were enumerated before any count was taken; the count in totals is computed, never chosen.

rows.name: Map identity and header records
rows.description: The per-area record the engine's own key lookup reads: 452 records of 56 bytes at 0x0808E2E0. Carries the two-byte map key the engine searches by, the metadata fields the SDK exposes, and pointers to the area's object arrays.
rows.evidence_authority: ROM bytes at 0x0808E2E0 and record 10 at 0x0808E510; consumer FUN_080089fc with stride 0x38 and the key-lookup literal 0x08008A58 = 0x0808E2E0; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:45-48
rows.read: All 452 records enumerate. The key, the five metadata fields the SDK names (zone, area, variation, flags, music_id) and the leading counts read. LOGII: a real 0x38-stride table exists at 0x08409368 with the same two-leading-byte key shape and ROM pointers in its +0x10/+0x14/+0x18 slots, and the profile deliberately does not declare it against this codec; field-level identity is UNKNOWN.
rows.edit: Five metadata fields are writable through tools/webfoot/maps.py set_field with a per-field range table; identity sharing is refused by measured exclusive-ownership checks. No Workbench surface calls set_field, so field editing is SDK and CLI only.
rows.author: New rows are authorable: the build re-emits the whole table above the original end, repoints the one literal the key lookup loads and raises the compiled row bound. Ceiling 58 appended rows, runtime-observed.
rows.xref: Inbound: the key lookup at 0x08008A58, the linear key scan in FUN_080089fc, the map list, the Atlas index. Outbound: the per-area object-array pointers and the trailing per-area pointer.
rows.validation_rebuild: Build re-emits the table and the compiled bound; project validate refuses an index-moving change by name. Byte-exact round trip of canonical records is proven by the profile reader.
rows.ui: Maps editor lists and renders every map; New map is a shipped surface. Field-level header editing has no UI.
rows.restrictions: Record fields +0x0C, +0x10, +0x18, +0x1C, +0x20, +0x24, +0x28, +0x30 and +0x34 are not modelled; the trigger semantics some tracked notes place at +0x04 and +0x10 are disputed (see map-event-trigger-records). New-row authoring is capped at 58 rows and an authored row inherits its donor.
rows.external_tool: hex editor for the unmodelled fields; Ghidra to settle the disputed offsets.
open_questions: Which of +0x0C..+0x34 are counts, pointers or flags?
Is the 0x08409368 LOGII table the same record family in a variant layout?

rows.name: Map layout chunk grids
rows.description: A map's layers and the fixed-size grid of four-byte chunk references inside each layer record, which is what the engine draws as the map's visible layout.
rows.evidence_authority: tools/webfoot/map_layout_edit.py:63-76; tests/integration/test_map_layout_editor_rom.py:56-58 (452/341/111); runtime observation recorded in src/data/capabilities.json:185 (tiles) and :219 (resize)
rows.read: All 452 maps and 1,808 layer slots enumerate; 1,516 slots are the dominant chunk-grid form. Cell values, layer pointers and classification are read and rendered.
rows.edit: 341 of 452 maps expose an editable layer; a cell is reassigned in place to another chunk the same layer already uses. Painting, undo and eyedropper are one history. 111 maps are refused for three named reasons: single-chunk dominant grids, absent dominant layers, forms outside the proven grid (screen-entry layers, the terrain-field form used by map 19, zero-dimension records).
rows.author: Growth only: a supported layer's grid may be enlarged and re-emitted above the original end with the layer-slot pointer repointed, and the map extent word raised. Shrinking is refused. One unused layer slot may be activated with a new supported visual layer.
rows.xref: Map identity to layer records to chunk containers; Atlas lists the layer and cell owners; the renderer resolves cells through the map's assembled character block.
rows.raw_range: Layer records and their grids are addressed per layer from the map root; no single table. The chunk-container table reached from the grid is row map-chunk-containers.
rows.validation_rebuild: Validate plus build; the application round-trip reopens the emitted image through its own manifest. Emulator validation of the layout-write capability itself was not performed; the painting and resize capabilities were.
rows.ui: Maps editor Layout mode: grid view, cell replacement, chunk chooser, resize form, layer list, Create Chunk.
rows.restrictions: The writable unit is a four-byte chunk reference, not a hardware tile. A layer that draws one chunk has nothing to paint with. No new graphics reach a layer: only arrangements of chunks the layer already draws. Authored grids are map-scoped. The runtime evidence on this row comes from the painted-cell authority, which writes the same four-byte cell and was observed after leaving and re-entering the area; the registry's layout capability separately records that emulator validation of its own single-operation write was not performed, so the two records must not be quoted as one.
rows.external_tool: tile editor plus a custom decoder for anything below the chunk: tileset entries, tile bits 12-15 and palettes outside the shared object palette.
open_questions: What do tile-map bits 12-15 mean (they are zero in all 3,834,880 canonical entries and are preserve-only)?

Map 19 uses the terrain-field layer form that the editor refuses; whether a background ever displays its composite plane is provisional and waits on a map-19 fixture, not on tooling (docs/research/ASSET_EXPORT_MAP19_VERIFICATION.md:380-449).

rows.name: Map chunk containers
rows.description: The engine's chunk resource: a 32x32 plane of 16-bit screen entries that a layout cell refers to by address. This is the level at which map graphics are composed in this engine.
rows.evidence_authority: tools/webfoot/map_chunk.py; docs/research/MAP_CHUNK_AUTHORING.md; runtime observation recorded in src/data/capabilities.json:195-211
rows.read: Chunk bodies are reached through the layer grid and are rendered; the chunk's 16-bit entries are decoded for display.
rows.edit: Existing chunks are readable but the shipped surface composes new ones rather than editing retail ones in place.
rows.author: A new chunk may be created from one a dominant layer already draws: its 32x32 plane is rearranged using only screen entries that same layer already displays, it gets its own project identity, and the build materialises it above the original ROM end. Runtime-observed: the engine's loaded BG1 tilemap carries the authored arrangement while BG0, BG2 and BG3 stay byte-identical.
rows.xref: Layer grid cell to chunk address; chunk to the map's assembled character block that resolves its tile ordinals.
rows.raw_range: Chunk bodies are addressed per map; a new body is emitted above the original ROM end through the allocator.
rows.validation_rebuild: Validate refuses an entry outside the layer's own vocabulary; build allocates and resolves the cell. Runtime-proven for the authored case.
rows.ui: Maps editor Layout mode: Create Chunk, chunk editor, chunk brush.
rows.restrictions: An authored chunk adds no tiles and no palettes: it is a new arrangement of graphics the map already draws. Chunks are map-scoped because their tile ordinals only resolve through one map's character block. Creation depends on generated expansion, since the canonical image declares 256 bytes of free space.
rows.external_tool: tile editor and a graphics codec writer for genuinely new artwork.
open_questions: Is a chunk body ever shared between maps, and what would make one portable?

rows.name: Map graphics: character blocks, tilesets and screen-entry planes
rows.description: The assembled graphics a map's chunk entries index: the character block, the tileset and the palettes a layer draws with. Distinct from chunk containers, which hold only references into this vocabulary.
rows.evidence_authority: tools/webfoot/formats/map_graphics.py; tools/webfoot/tileset_compositor.py; tools/research/domain_reachability.py:366 (proven render for maps 39 and 40 only); tools/webfoot/cli.py:618-643
rows.read: The tileset census and atlas commands enumerate a map's graphics, and the compositor renders them. The proven render path covers maps 39 and 40; the general case is not proven, which is the main limit on this row's read side.
rows.edit: None. No SDK writer addresses a tileset or a character-block entry.
rows.author: None. No shipped surface composes new tiles or tilesets.
rows.xref: Chunk to character block; the map record to its graphics; Atlas carries the owners.
rows.raw_range: Character-block and tileset bodies are addressed per map; the renderer resolves them from the map record.
rows.validation_rebuild: Not applicable at this state: there is no write path to validate.
rows.ui: Maps editor Layout mode renders chunk cells; there is no tile or tileset surface.
rows.restrictions: Read coverage itself is partial: proven for two maps. Tile-map bits 12-15 are zero in every canonical entry and must be preserved by any future writer, which needs no semantics. Palettes are shared with the object palette system.
rows.external_tool: standalone tile or graphics editor plus a custom decoder; the compressed container format also needs the encoder that row compression-codec covers.
open_questions: What is the full map-graphics load list, and why does only maps 39/40 render?

rows.name: Per-area counted object array tables
rows.description: The engine loads four independent counted arrays per area, each reached through the map record's +0x04 pointer: a count byte per family in the pointed-to structure and an array pointer per family at +0x14 (stride 4), +0x18 (stride 4), +0x1C (stride 4) and +0x20 (stride 8). This is the structural answer to what the unmodelled sibling records are.
rows.evidence_authority: FUN_08008b30 decompilation and the inline walk at 0x08008C9E..0x08008CAE; ROM bytes at 0x08008CA2 (ldrb r0,[r0,#0x4]) and 0x08008CAC (ldr r0,[r0,#0x14]); docs/research/BUU_MAP_OBJECT_ARRAYS.md
rows.read: One of the four arrays is enumerated and rendered by the product. The existence of the other three is proven, but the product has no reader for their elements.
rows.edit: Array +0x14 is editable through the placement surfaces. Arrays +0x18, +0x1C and +0x20 have no reader and no writer.
rows.author: Clone-only for array +0x14, ceiling 255 object slots per map. The other three arrays have no authoring path.
rows.xref: Map record +0x04 to the object block; the object block's four counts and array pointers; placement records to the sprite resolver and the enemy stat table.
rows.raw_range: The array pointers are per area; the map-10 array is at file 0x07293C. No fixed table bounds the whole family.
rows.validation_rebuild: Array +0x14 writing validates and builds and is runtime-proven. The other three arrays participate in no validation because nothing writes them.
rows.ui: Maps editor Objects mode and the Scene editor both operate on array +0x14 only.
rows.restrictions: Structure confidence on the count bytes and on the pointed-to structure's base is PARTIAL rather than PROVEN: the decompiled walk dereferences map+0x04 before reading a count, while a tracked note places counts directly on the map record, and the same lane that produced the four-array claim separately found the 0x08008B30 map-loader attribution wrong, so the four-array model is INFERRED and disputed rather than settled. Three of four families are unmodelled, which is the largest single map-system coverage gap found. The row's writable cell is shared: the write path named in edit is the placement path of row placement-records, and the aggregate rule prints a shared-path caveat for it.
rows.external_tool: Ghidra to decode the element types of the +0x18, +0x1C and +0x20 families; hex editor to read them now.
open_questions: What are the +0x18, +0x1C and +0x20 arrays: warps, spawns, triggers, decorations?
Is the count byte base the map record or the structure +0x04 points at?

rows.name: Placement-family object records
rows.description: The object family the SDK models, reached from the first per-area array: records whose lead word is the constructor wrapper 0x0800FD55 and which carry a sprite id read at +0x10 and handed to the sprite-id resolver.
rows.evidence_authority: ROM bytes at 0x0800FD55 and the constructor FUN_0800f68c; the field read at 0x0800F6AE (ldr r0,[r5,#0x10]) and the call at 0x0800F6B0; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:34-44
rows.read: Placements enumerate per map with their stored signed position; supported types are classified; unsupported types render read-only.
rows.edit: Position moves through the proven signed map-pixel contract with an explicit signed-16 guard. Runtime-proven.
rows.author: Clone-only: an authored entity is a configured clone of a supported existing type; 268 maps are clone-capable; 255 slots per map is the ceiling because the count is one byte.
rows.xref: Placement to sprite identity (identity of the drawn sprite is not proven), placement to behaviour attachment, placement to the enemy stat table through the factory's literal 0x0800FD75 = 0x08711274.
rows.raw_range: Records are scattered across the object-array span from file 0x0728FC upward; no contiguous table and no stride: the codec is factory-led and variable-length.
rows.validation_rebuild: Validate plus build; the authored entity and its slot resolution are runtime-proven.
rows.ui: Maps editor Objects mode; Scene editor opened from the placement.
rows.restrictions: Clone-only authoring. Placement-to-sprite identity is not proven, so markers are neutral and browsing cannot say which sprite an object uses. The profile declares placement selector maximum 149 while the independently verified enemy-stat extent is 141 records, so selectors 141..149 name targets outside any verified codec.
rows.external_tool: Ghidra for the unmodelled fields and the enemy-to-sprite link; hex editor otherwise.
open_questions: Which fields of a placement record beyond the sprite id and position are read by the engine?
What resolves an enemy's sprite at runtime?
The construction site writes actor+0x1A0 with 40 of 40 rows matched, while the vertical field actor+0x1A4 and the facing selector 0x03001A34 are unproven: a fresh-map-load run would close them.

rows.name: Unmodelled sibling object record families (two families)
rows.description: Two further object families sharing the per-area array mechanism: records whose lead words are 0x08017DA3 (191 sprite-bearing records reported) and 0x080111A9 (148 reported), the third family at that address family being the placements of the row placement-records. Each is proven to load one field and call the same sprite resolver.
rows.evidence_authority: ROM disassembly at 0x08017DA6 (ldr r0,[r0,#0x10]; bl 0x08000158) and 0x080111AC (ldr r0,[r0,#0xc]; bl 0x08000158); counts from docs/research/BUU_MAP_OBJECT_ARRAYS.md:36-48, which proves three leading words over 1,898 slots, and are not re-derived
rows.read: No product reader. The sprite id field offset is proven for each family (+0x10 and +0x0C) and nothing else is decoded.
rows.edit: None.
rows.author: None.
rows.xref: Both families call the sprite-id resolver FUN_08000158; the containing array is one of the three unmodelled per-area arrays.
rows.raw_range: Not bounded. No stride and no table were found for either family.
rows.validation_rebuild: Not applicable: no write path exists.
rows.ui: None.
rows.restrictions: The record lengths, the record counts and every field except the sprite id are unknown for both families, which is why the state is UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED rather than KNOWN_BUT_UNSUPPORTED: a proven field offset is not a proven boundary. The counts 191 and 148 come from tracked research and were not re-derived in this census.

open_questions: What are these families: decorations, projectiles, interactive props, spawn points?
Which per-area array reaches each one, and what bounds either family's records?

rows.edit: None.

rows.name: Enemy and character stat records
rows.description: The 141-record, 28-byte stat table the placement factory indexes: a per-record id field, a shared pointer and a per-record pointer into a variable pool.
rows.evidence_authority: ROM bytes at 0x08711274 with the recurring pointer at a 7-word period; the base literal 0x0801BA90 = 0x08711274; tools/webfoot/stats.py; tools/webfoot/formats/stat_tables.py; tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml:49-52
rows.read: All 141 records of 28 bytes enumerate with field decode, round-trip and a CLI listing.
rows.edit: Fields are rewritable in place through the SDK and its CLI, and the packaged enemy randomizer rewrites fields in place with a changed-field list. No Workbench surface reaches the stat tables, and no capability in the registry names them.
rows.author: Not meaningful: the count is fixed and no growth path for a stat record is claimed.
rows.xref: Placement factory to stat table; enemy stats to the character-sprite table is NOT established: no enemy record holds a pointer into the graphics regions and no field indexes the 297-entry table, so the selection happens in code.
rows.validation_rebuild: Stat round-trip tests exist; in-place field writes build into the image. A LOGII stat codec does not exist and the profile states no LOGII table matches these record shapes.
rows.ui: None in the Workbench; the packaged enemy randomizer has its own window.
rows.restrictions: Field semantics are named by the product for the fields it models: tools/webfoot/stats.py:76-93 defines the enemy fields exp, hp, level, strength, power and endurance, with level bounded 1..200 from a disassembled comparison in the experience award path, and stats.py:231 exposes a lookup by hp. The residual gaps are the unnamed pointer and pool fields, the byte pairs, and the absence of runtime proof that an edited value is consumed. The profile declares placement selector maximum 149 while this extent holds 141 records, so selectors 141..149 point outside any verified codec. Runtime evidence is PARTIAL and the gap is named: the enemy randomizer's recorded runs read the engine's own MapEntry+0x14 slots and two reward counters, but the record states the run does not read a constructed actor.
rows.external_tool: Ghidra to name the fields through the damage formula; mGBA debugger to confirm a changed value is read.
open_questions: Which field feeds the damage formula?

rom_surface.source: Re-measured by this census from a local clone of the public Buu's Fury reconstruction at commit 5a6d3349199d16b1800d55d200bcbf2f8d91b29e, config/rom_map.json, whose 249 region lengths sum to 8,388,608. The reconstruction is a lower evidence rung than the bytes; its classes are used as a classification and each class names who decided it.

classes.class: executable code, identified but not semantically reconstructed
classes.decided_by: reconstruction region map, code plus code_candidate classes; corroborated by the Ghidra program's disassembly
classes.note: The reconstruction credits 5,088 of 186,346 tracked executable bytes semantically. The Ghidra program reports 85,181 functions over the whole image, which is not a code count.

classes.class: known structured data declared by the product
classes.decided_by: reconstruction region map, pointer_table, lookup_table, palette and strings classes, which contain the nine tables tools/webfoot/data/roms.yaml declares
classes.note: Semantic ownership is established for the declared subset. Ownership of the rest of this class is not established, and a class is not a claim about every byte in it.

classes.decided_by: reconstruction region map, compressed_asset class at medium confidence
classes.note: Identified as an asset span, not reconstructed as a format; 3,035,864 bytes of it is the sprite container span at 0x083C34D0. No audio span is identified in any class.

classes.decided_by: reconstruction region map, padding class at proven confidence (0x087B89A8..0x08800000)
classes.note: The tail. 516 unresolved candidate references target this region, which is why only a carved 256-byte window inside it is declared free.

classes.decided_by: reconstruction region map, unknown class plus the library_data and structured_data regions, which are moved here because they are refuted or uncertified (see caveats)
classes.note: This is where deeper reverse engineering would most improve editor coverage. The largest single region is 937,984 bytes at 0x0945C0. 101 unknown regions carry confidence unknown and 73 low.
The 192-byte GBA header, read and checksum-validated by the product.

caveats: An incbin region is not automatically unknown: this classification separates identified-but-unreconstructed from unidentified.

Four region classifications were re-checked against the bytes and refuted, so those classes carry no independent certification: library_signal_strings at file 0x7B71A2 is a 2,050-byte signed-16-bit curve and not strings; file 0x03D4D0 labelled ARM decodes as clean Thumb; the region at 0x0871D1E0 holds signed data, not only pointers; and the map-loader attribution at 0x08008B30 is wrong.
A file offset and an image identity are a measurement convention, not an engine fact; both static lanes map offset 0 to 0x08000000 and the engine was not consulted.
Two static instruments agreeing is a consistency check, not corroboration, when the question is causal.

totals.computed_by: docs/research/rom_editor_coverage.json is validated by tests/unit/test_rom_editor_coverage.py, which recomputes every count in this block from rows[].games and fails on any difference. No count here is authored by hand.

v1_triage.why: Without it, a hex editor writes bytes the product cannot attribute, and the raw browser cannot answer what owns a range.

v1_triage.gap: A container encoder that can grow a filtered or packed payload.
v1_triage.why: It gates every insertion capability: new graphics, new dialogue text, new sprite payloads. Named in the roadmap as the Phase 3/4 gate.

v1_triage.gap: Stat-table and map-header surfaces over the SDK models that already exist.
v1_triage.why: The SDK reads and writes these domains today and the product neither names nor surfaces them, so the claim to be a general-purpose editor is materially overstated without them. This is surfacing plus registry honesty, not new research.

v1_triage.gap: Patch export and modified-range visualisation in the desktop shell.
v1_triage.why: Both services exist and are verified; the remaining cost is a surface.

v1_triage.gap: The three unmodelled per-area object arrays and their record families.
v1_triage.why: Three of four engine-owned object families are invisible to the product. Until element types are decoded the editor cannot scope them, and the decoding is cheap because the consumer function is already decompiled.

v1_triage.gap: The save format and whether expansion preserves it.
v1_triage.why: A 16 MiB generated image is shipped as a product path with no save-compatibility argument. This is a correctness risk before it is a feature.

v1_triage.gap: Audio: locate the engine, the tables and the sequence or sample data.
v1_triage.why: An entire row is unknown, and the instrument could not search for it. Editor scoping is impossible today.

v1_triage.gap: The game-level meaning of the 266 script native handlers.
v1_triage.why: It blocks general script authoring and all LOGII dialogue, and it is the shared unknown behind several rows.
Real gaps with no format yet. Valuable expansions, safe to defer.

v1_triage.gap: Map graphics below the chunk level, and tileset authoring.
v1_triage.why: The chunk-level surface already covers ordinary map hacking; tile-level work needs the encoder first.

v1_triage.gap: A dedicated editor for the compiler-embedded assertion strings, the colour lookup block and the debug debris.
v1_triage.why: Real ROM internals that need no editor surface: a semantic or raw browser covers them.
